scope: Working-tree diff against 38918e2: assets/reference/README.md, docs/accounting.md, docs/design-system.md, docs/governance.md, docs/localization.md, docs/testing.md, docs/ui-patterns.md, governance.json, justfile, .agents/skills and tool/*
Pinned tool bundle tool/ledger-tooling-v0.1.0.tar.gz, tool/tooling.lock.json and the generated tool/bootstrap.go compared byte for byte against the ledger-tooling producer working tree
changes classification output for the current App change set and for scratch documentation-only and asset-data edits
Removal of the unconfigured mutation recipe and the documentation statements that replace it
New skills-check gate step in governance.json and the justfile recipe
Base-to-working governance.json comparison for removed or weakened check steps

findings.rule: The pinned tool bundle must match the producer working tree and both consumers must pin the same archive digest
findings.trigger: The pinned archive had been superseded by producer edits, so the executed classifier and gate policy were older than the ledger-tooling working tree
findings.impact: The App enforced a stale procedure: CRLF-normalised skill comparison, nested-template rejection, --include= and whole-repository gate detection, command_migrations and stricter step identity were absent from the tool that actually ran
findings.recommendation: Re-bundle and re-pin; verified sha256 5639509aad4db9cd81d98d5918971acf91b6e3fcb4f39d16d50ae73bf6d27906 equals the SHA-256 of tool/ledger-tooling-v0.1.0.tar.gz in both ledger-app and ledger, every archive entry is byte-equal to the ledger-tooling working tree, the archive contains only .go/.md/go.mod source, and tool/bootstrap.go equals the bundled bootstrap/bootstrap.go plus exactly one generated header line

findings.rule: Skill comparison must not treat line-ending conversion as drift
findings.trigger: A core.autocrlf=true checkout materialises unchanged skill content with CRLF endings, and this repository is validated on a Windows runner
findings.impact: skills-check failed for an untouched file, so the Windows leg of the quality matrix could not pass without editing a correct file
findings.recommendation: normalizeEndings now maps CRLF to LF on both sides; reproduced in a /tmp scratch copy: CRLF-ised ledger-debug and ledger-architecture-review copies pass (exit 0, standalone and as a step inside a configured command) while a one-word content change still fails with skill copy has drifted from the pinned template

findings.rule: A documentation-only change must not request UI capture evidence
findings.trigger: The classifier set visual for any assets/ path before testing whether the file was documentation, so an edited README under assets/ demanded before and after captures
findings.impact: A correct documentation change could not satisfy the CI visual gate, which required UI capture evidence for a text edit
findings.recommendation: Classification now derives doc from the .md/.txt extension and only sets ui, visual and native when the path is not documentation; verified the current App change set reports visual:false, a scratch assets/reference/README.md-only edit reports visual:false, docs/testing.md alone reports visual:false, and a scratch non-documentation assets/reference/locale_rules.json edit still reports visual:true so the rule is not vacuous

findings.rule: Every advertised recipe must invoke a command the pinned tool and policy actually implement
findings.trigger: The mutation recipe invoked a command that neither the pinned CLI implements nor governance.json configures
findings.impact: just --list advertised a quality gate that could not run, so a blocked mutation signal could be mistaken for a covered one
findings.recommendation: Recipe removed and replaced by skills-check; just --list in ledger-app advertises no mutation recipe, governance.json configures no mutation command, docs/governance.md states that mutation coverage is blocked with no recipe pretending to run one, and a script cross-check of every recipe in both repositories found no invocation of an unconfigured command

findings.rule: A correction round must add gate coverage rather than remove it
findings.trigger: The shared check command was edited in the same change that re-pinned the bundle
findings.impact: An unreviewed removal of a gate step or command would silently weaken the repository gate
findings.recommendation: Compared git show 38918e2:governance.json with the working tree: check gained exactly the @ledger-tool skills-check step, and no command, step, coverage threshold, source root, exclusion, inventory or baseline field changed; policy-check exits 0

limitations: Local-only delivery by explicit user decision: no remote push, no hosted CI run, no branch protection or release verification was exercised
Flutter and Dart suites, native device flows and the Linux and Windows GitHub runner legs were not executed; all local execution was on the macOS host
Reviewer identity and independence are asserted by the review harness, not cryptographically proven; review-check validates schema, fingerprint freshness and non-blocking severities only
The reviewer did not run just check, dart analyze, flutter test, coverage, generate-check or capture-ui, and produced no UI capture evidence; no hosted runner or device result is established

Classification and skills-check experiments were run against scratch copies under /tmp; every repository was confirmed byte-identical by SHA-256 manifest before and after, and both fingerprints were recomputed unchanged at review time

ledger-tooling is a live working tree concurrently edited by another reviewer agent and exercised by a concurrent just check; bundle freshness was re-verified after those edits but the producer may move again
go run based CLI checks passed locally; this does not establish hosted CI, device, visual-capture or coverage results for the App
